title: Soft Launch Capsule: Concierge Onboarding Kit (sketch)
content:
Context / why this exists:

We onboard a lot of developers who try the Redwood API once or twice and then drop off because they hit integration friction: missing examples for their stack, unclear cost trade-offs for ephemeral endpoints, and no fast path to production-quality defaults (batching, retries, prompt templates). We should ship a small, opinionated package — the "Soft Launch Capsule" — that gives a one-click (well, one-clone) path from signup -> hello-world -> basic canary in prod.

Goal (non-committal):
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-integration (TTFSI) from ~45m to <10m for new devs trying hosted API.
- Surface revenue-signals earlier: increase demo-to-pay conversion by surfacing a recommended dedicated plan after 3k tokens.
- Collect higher-quality telemetry on integration friction so we can iterate on SDKs and docs.

What the Capsule includes (first iteration):
1) SDK starter repo (node + python): minimal app with config skeleton, pre-built prompt templates for common patterns (chat, summarize, extract), example environment setups for serverless and containerized apps.
2) Prebaked prompts and temperature presets: conservative/creative/structured modes with suggested token limits.
3) A tiny local dev harness that runs a small smoke test (local) and a token-usage preview that simulates cost for a session.
4) Canary config file: a one-line toggle in the repo to enable "capsule-canary" route in our hosted API that gives devs an SLA-lite but throttled soft-path for demos.
5) UX: sample UI components (React) that show streaming responses + token meter + fallback toggles.
6) Observability hooks: suggested events/metrics and a sample small dashboard (Grafana / console link) that shows latency, cost, error rate.

User stories (raw):
- As a frontend dev, I want a drop-in chat widget I can paste into a static site so I can demo the product to my PM within 10 minutes.
- As an engineer exploring cost, I want a simulation of likely monthly token spend if I scale to 1k DAU so I can propose a budget.
- As an SDK user, I want a canary flag that uses rate-limited demo capacity so I don't accidentally use production quota during an internal demo.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- The starter repo boots in <5 minutes with clear README and 3 runnable examples (chat, summarize, search rerank).
- The canary toggle maps to an existing internal routing policy and enforces a 10rps limit and lower throughput pool.
- The UI component streams tokens using our streaming API and displays the token meter (approx cost) live.
- Demo telemetry produced: first_success_event, smoke_test_passed, canary_toggle_used, sample_token_estimate.

Soft rollout plan (sketch):
- Phase A (internal): engineers + solutions engs (10 people) try the capsule, collect feedback.
- Phase B (invite-only): 100 PLG signups in a week get an in-app prompt: "Try our quick demo kit" with optional opt-in. Track TTFSI/engagement.
- Phase C (public): surfacing the capsule on quickstarts, templates, and new-account email.

Telemetry & metrics we need to instrument: 
- TTFSI (time from signup -> first successful API call via capsule).
- Repo clone -> smoke test success rate.
- Average tokens used per session in first 7 days.
- Percent of users who flip canary -> request dedicated plan.
- Errors by step (install, env, run, api key).

Engineering constraints & rough effort estimate: 
- SDK starter repo: 2 wk (1 eng + 0.5 pd).
- React widget: 1 wk (0.5 eng + design).
- Canary backend routing: 1 wk (infra routing + policy).
- Telemetry dashboard + events: 1 wk (SRE + product).
- Total: ~4–5 weeks to a basic public-ready capsule.

Open questions / risks (brain-dump):
- How to ensure the canary pool can't be abused by mass signups? Need rate-limiting and per-account throttles. Add captcha / email gating for invite.
- Legal/compliance: Will the demo data leak into customer logs for hosted? We should default to ephemeral logs and a clear checkbox for debug logs.
- Pricing clarity: showing a projected cost estimate could scare users; must be framed as "estimate" and include a link to cost optimization tips.
- Dev velocity: this almost duplicates some starter repos in OSS; check OSS-first approach vs in-house.

Proposed experiment matrix (A/B ideas):
- A: Capsule onboarding prompt immediately after signup vs B: capsule suggested after first successful API call. Metric: TTFSI reduction, engagement.
- A: Show cost-estimate inline vs B: show only after user uses >500 tokens. Metric: conversion to sign-up + support tickets.

Docs / README outline (very rough):
- Quickstart (1-minute): what to paste to show chat on a static page.
- 5-minute: run sample app and smoke test.
- 15-minute: customize prompts + toggle canary to test scaling.
- Troubleshooting: common env errors, common network/firewall issues for private deployments.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Pull in a short legal blurb about ephemeral logging and analytics (ask Legal: @Evan Park).
- Ask Solutions Eng to add 2 customer-facing demo scripts for finance and product teams.
- Prototype the token meter UI as a separate small package for reuse.
- Add a small checklist in Console: "Install capsule -> Run smoke test -> Enable canary".

Slack threads / references: 
- SRE: #infra-canary-pools (ask about quota enforcement)
- DX: #devexp-quickstarts (coordinate SDKs and templates)

Small mock flow (developer POV):
1) Sign up, click "Try Soft Launch Capsule"
2) Create API key (scoped) -> click "Clone Starter Repo"
3) npm install && npm run smoke (app hits /capsule-canary route)
4) UI loads chat widget, shows token meter; dev toggles demo -> runs 3 queries
5) Console shows smoke_test_passed event; suggestions card: "Consider dedicated tier after 3k tokens/month"

If we like traction: future ideas (parking lot):
- Integrations: prebuilt snippets for Vercel Edge Functions, Cloudflare Workers, and Netlify.
- Guided walkthrough with code-tour in repo.
- Marketplace of prompt templates curated by use-case.
- One-click deploy to a sandboxed dedicated capacity for enterprise evals.

Delivery notes: keep this intentionally lightweight and opinionated. Capsule should be opinionated on defaults (batching off by default? per-request cache suggestions?) but configurable. The win is in making the demo frictionless and making the first successful integration feel like a win for the developer.

-- Juliette
